headline: NEW to scans -- Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport reopens two terminals Sunday Oct 25 under a new domestic/international'
dek: Terminal 1 is designated for domestic flights and Terminal 2 for international flights operated by national carriers, effective Sunday Oct 25, 2026. Passengers with confirmed bookings must verify flight status with their airlines before travelling.
sources: King Khalid International Airport statement on X (@KKIASA), via Arab News and Times of Israel
fault_line: Is Riyadh reopening because the threat has eased, or is it a defiant partial reopening while foreign carriers still refuse to fly?

sections.what_happened: Terminal 1 is designated for domestic flights and Terminal 2 for international flights operated by national carriers, effective Sunday Oct 25, 2026. Passengers with confirmed bookings must verify flight status with their airlines before travelling. Arab News frames it as reopening two terminals two weeks after the Oct 10 Ansar Allah missile strike that killed 13 and wounded 300+.
sections.what_verified: 2 distinct publisher families: Arab News T3 (airport statement + Oct 10 casualty context) and Times of Israel T3 (airport X statement). Türkiye Today/ARN carry the same airport notice (not counted as extra families beyond the notice itself).
sections.what_disputed: The notice covers national carriers only; it does not say foreign carriers resume, and several Gulf/foreign carriers remain grounded beyond Oct 25 (Emirates holds to Oct 25, flydubai cancels to Oct 29, Etihad holds Riyadh/Dammam to Nov 5, per MinuteMirror Oct 24 roundup). 'Resume' framing overstates a partial, national-carrier-only reopening; Ansar Allah strikes on Saudi airports continued through Oct 24 (Saree claims incl. Riyadh airport, Oct 24).
sections.why_matters: Two weeks after 13 people died at this airport, Riyadh reopens -- but only for Saudi airlines. Foreign carriers are still staying away. What does that split tell you about who believes it is safe?
sections.context: Background: NEW to scans (in-window corroboration + missed catch-up) -- Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport reopens two terminals Sunday Oct 25 under a new domestic/international split for national carriers, two weeks after the deadly Oct 10 Ansar Allah missile strike

totw_analysis: Our read: Two weeks after 13 people died at this airport, Riyadh reopens -- but only for Saudi airlines. Foreign carriers are still staying away. What does that split tell you about who believes it is safe? The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is Riyadh reopening because the threat has eased, or is it a defiant partial reopening while foreign carriers still refuse to fly?
